results.mainTitle: Abstract 13385: Prediction of Patient Comfort for Extravascular and Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillation Devices Using Modeling
descriptions: <jats:p>             <jats:bold>Introduction:</jats:bold>             Implanted medical devices may exert pressure on patients’ tissues, generating discomfort. Depending on implant location and device design, the pressure generated will vary. The investigational extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (EV ICD) device volume is 33 cubic centimeters (cc), while the commercially available subcutaneous (SQ) ICD is 59 cc. The objective of this work is to compare the pressure on the subcutaneous and muscular tissue over a device in a tissue pocket through computer simulation.           </jats:p>           <jats:p>             <jats:bold>Method:</jats:bold>             Finite element modeling was performed for the EV ICD and SQ ICD in three implant locations: subcutaneous, submuscular, and intermuscular. A pocket condition was simulated with tissue above the device being displaced by the thickness of the device; the resulting pressures were calculated. Device contact pressure on the subcutaneous and muscular tissue above the device was used as a surrogate for potential patient discomfort caused by the device pushing against tissue.           </jats:p>           <jats:p>             <jats:bold>Results:</jats:bold>             In all three implant locations, the tissue pressure of the EV ICD was lower than that of the SQ ICD. Larger areas of high pressure were present on the tissue surface near the edges of the SQ ICD device compared to the EV ICD. The reduction observed in the EV ICD relative to the SQ ICD device was 24% in subcutaneous, 12% in submuscular, and 44% in intermuscular. See figure.           </jats:p>           <jats:p>             <jats:bold>Conclusion:</jats:bold>             Simulation shows that the EV ICD exerts less pressure on the tissue over the device than the SQ ICD across clinically relevant locations, with the potential to improve patient comfort.           </jats:p>           <jats:p>             <jats:graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="g13385.jpg" />           </jats:p>
